Automatically try a backup model when the primary is overloaded or briefly unavailable
The fallback reuses the same provider, protocol and API key. Rate limits (429), server errors (5xx) and timeouts fall back automatically; an invalid key (401/403) is reported and never cascades.
The assistant could not get an answer: %1$s
Save tokens, battery and CPU for overnight runs

When on, the assistant asks for shorter answers and gathers less background-research context, and background polling relaxes during quiet hours (00:00–06:00) when no task is running. Never disables a feature you started.
Assemble prompts from AGENTS.md and workspace context

When on, the coding agent reads AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md) from the active workspace as data and merges it into prompts; the assembled prompt is versioned. Off by default — when off, prompts are sent unchanged. AGENTS.md is always treated as data, never as system instructions.
Saved prompts you can run manually or on a schedule

Automatic failover between models and providers
On a transient failure, try the next compatible model or provider instead of stopping.
A turn that already ran tools is never re-run automatically, and API keys never leave secure storage. Only providers with a saved key are used.

Fall back to an on-device or LAN model server (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio)

The local model is tried only after the primary and fallback models fail with a transient error (rate limit, server error or timeout). The URL must be a local or private address — no API key is sent to it. Pull the model first, e.g. ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b.
Connect external or local tools the Sidekick assistant can call

A server is only contacted when you tap Test or when the assistant invokes a tool. HTTPS is used for external servers; plain HTTP is allowed only for local or private addresses. The assistant never sends your provider API key to a server — only the optional per-server token below.
